    AI Overview
    Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU)
     is a premier urban research university in Richmond, VA, renowned for its top-ranked School of the Arts, elite health sciences programs, and NCAA Division I basketball. Classified as a Carnegie Tier 1 research institution, it is recognized for innovation, a diverse and creative student body, and strong community engagement. 
    Key Recognitions and Strengths: 
    • Top-Tier Arts School: VCU School of the Arts is ranked fourth in the country, with its sculpture program ranked number one.
    • Health Sciences and Medicine: As a major academic medical center, VCU is known for dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, and the School of Medicine, which drives substantial research funding
      .
    • Research Innovation: VCU is a top 50 public research university and is recognized among the top 30 most innovative public universities, according to Visit Richmond VA and VCU News.
    • Urban Campus Environment: Integrated directly into downtown Richmond, the campus is known for its eclectic, creative, and inclusive atmosphere.
    • Rams Basketball: VCU is known for its high-profile NCAA Tournament appearances, including a 2011 Final Four run, says The Fayetteville Observer. 
    Notable Areas of Excellence: 
    • STEM and Healthcare: Strong focus on interdisciplinary work, such as collaborating on medicine and engineering, notes VCU News.
    • Community Engagement: Ranked highly for its commitment to community, according to VCU About.
    • Creative Economy: A hub for artists, entrepreneurs, and nonprofit leaders, says VCU Why VCU.

      The VCU Police Department is bringing back a fan-favorite initiative to help address a key issue on campus: pedestrian safety. On Tuesday, March 17, VCU Police officers dressed as referees, and sporting whistles and flags, will be out on VCU’s Monroe Park Campus to draw attention to unsafe pedestrian habits and engage community members on the issue. VCU Police led a similar initiative in 2023. Officers will flag pedestrian “fouls” in a light-hearted manner, distribute travel safety material and award those who cross appropriately with prizes. Pedestrian safety remains a top focus for VCU Police, VCU, VCU Health and community partners. Travelers are encouraged to practice safe habits every time they move through campus or the city by eliminating distractions and remaining alert. Read more: https://news.vcu.edu/article/vcupd-referees-hit-the-streets-for-pedestrian-safety

      Tiffany Gary has a message for VCU alums on the fence about attending April’s Black Alumni Weekend: You’ll be missing out if you stay home. That’s because this year’s signature weekend, April 23-26, includes more events, and organizers expect more alums than ever before to come to campus to reminisce and celebrate culture, community and the power of VCU connections. In fact, since 2021 when the celebration was virtual because of the COVID pandemic, attendance has more than doubled, from 454 alums registered in 2022, to more than 1,100 who came to last year’s weekend. “Every year we keep going and going and getting bigger,” said Gary, a 2000 VCU graduate who chairs the VCU Black Alumni Council Programs and Events Committee that leads the alumni weekend planning. “We really have rounded out the weekend to be not just the same old thing. We try to add a little bit of variety every year, so that if you came last year, you’re going to miss out if you don’t come this year.” Read more: ht

      Description

      Virginia Commonwealth University is a public research university in Richmond, Virginia, United States. VCU was founded in 1838 as the medical department of Hampden–Sydney College, becoming the Medical College of Virginia in 1854. Wikipedia
      Address: Richmond, VA 23284
      Campus: Midsize city, 150 acres (0.61 km2)
      Acceptance rate: 92.6% (2024) IPEDS
      Students: 28,919 (2021–22)
      Undergraduate tuition and fees: In-state tuition 16,458 USD, Out-of-state tuition 39,042 USD (2023 – 24) IPEDS
      Mascot: Rodney the Ram
      Founded: 1838
      Provost: Arturo Saavedra (interim)
      Endowment: $3.23 billion (2025)
      Colors: Black and gold;
      Accreditation: SACS
      President: Michael Rao
      Phone: (804) 828-0100
